records.name: Embedding Scripts within Scripts
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An adversary leverages the capability to execute their own script by embedding it within other scripts that the target software is likely to execute due to programs' vulnerabilities that are brought on by allowing remote hosts to execute scripts.

records.name: Leverage Executable Code in Non-Executable Files
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An attack of this type exploits a system's trust in configuration and resource files. When the executable loads the resource (such as an image file or configuration file) the attacker has modified the file to either execute malicious code directly or manipulate the target process (e.g. application server) to execute based on the malicious configuration parameters. Since systems are increasingly interrelated mashing up resources from local and remote sources the possibility of this attack occurring is high.

records.name: Embed Virus into DLL
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An adversary tampers with a DLL and embeds a computer virus into gaps between legitimate machine instructions. These gaps may be the result of compiler optimizations that pad memory blocks for performance gains. The embedded virus then attempts to infect any machine which interfaces with the product, and possibly steal private data or eavesdrop.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:2
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Utilize strict type, character, and encoding enforcement.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:3
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Server side developers should not proxy content via XHR or other means. If a HTTP proxy for remote content is setup on the server side, the client's browser has no way of discerning where the data is originating from.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:4
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Ensure all content that is delivered to client is sanitized against an acceptable content specification.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:5
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Perform input validation for all remote content.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:6
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Perform output validation for all remote content.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:7
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Disable scripting languages such as JavaScript in browser

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:9
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Patching software. There are many attack vectors for XSS on the client side and the server side. Many vulnerabilities are fixed in service packs for browser, web servers, and plug in technologies, staying current on patch release that deal with XSS countermeasures mitigates this.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:1
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Use browser technologies that do not allow client side scripting.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:19:mitigation:10
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Privileges are constrained, if a script is loaded, ensure system runs in chroot jail or other limited authority mode

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:35:mitigation:1
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Design: Enforce principle of least privilege

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:35:mitigation:2
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Design: Run server interfaces with a non-root account and/or utilize chroot jails or other configuration techniques to constrain privileges even if attacker gains some limited access to commands.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:35:mitigation:3
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Implementation: Perform testing such as pen-testing and vulnerability scanning to identify directories, programs, and interfaces that grant direct access to executables.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:35:mitigation:4
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Implementation: Implement host integrity monitoring to detect any unwanted altering of configuration files.

related.name: capec:attack-pattern:35:mitigation:5
related.label: Mitigation
related.description: Implementation: Ensure that files that are not required to execute, such as configuration files, are not over-privileged, i.e. not allowed to execute.

related.name: Hiding Malicious Data or Code within Files
related.label: AttackPattern
related.description: Files on various operating systems can have a complex format which allows for the storage of other data, in addition to its contents. Often this is metadata about the file, such as a cached thumbnail for an image file. Unless utilities are invoked in a particular way, this data is not visible during the normal use of the file. It is possible for an attacker to store malicious data or code using these facilities, which would be difficult to discover.
